title: Sea ahead, army behind. We are caught.
subtitle: The moment every exit looked closed
then: When the two groups saw each other, Musa's companions said {trap}we are sure to be overtaken.{/trap} Ibn Kathir explains why: they were on the shore of the sea, with {trap}the sea ahead and Fir'awn's troops behind.{/trap} One of them asked Musa if this was really where Allah told him to bring them.
now: The rent is due, the account is empty, and the phone is ringing with a number you do not want to answer. Every road you can see is closed. {idea}What you can see is not everything there is.{/idea}
old: If I cannot see a way out, there is none.
new: Allah's way out is often the one I cannot see yet.
try: Write down your situation that feels like a dead end. Under it write: Allah sees a way.

title: No. My Lord is with me. He will guide me.
subtitle: Musa's certainty at the water's edge

row.title: No
sub: what you fear will not happen

then: Musa says {idea}no, my Lord is with me, He will guide me.{/idea} Ibn Kathir explains: nothing you fear will happen to you, for {reward}Allah commanded me to bring you here, and He does not go back on His promise.{/reward} Musa did not yet know how. He knew Who.
now: You do not have the plan. You do not know how the bills will be paid or how the diagnosis ends. {reward}You can still say: my Lord is with me, He will guide me.{/reward} You do not need the whole map to take the next step.
old: I cannot feel calm until I know exactly how this works out.
new: I can be calm knowing Who is with me, even before I know how.
try: When panic rises today, say quietly: my Lord is with me, He will guide me.

title: Strike the sea. It splits into mountains of water.
subtitle: The way opens through the obstacle itself
then: As the army drew close, Allah told Musa to strike the sea, and {idea}it parted, each side like a huge mountain.{/idea} Ibn Abbas said it split into {reward}twelve paths, one for each tribe{/reward}, and Ibn Kathir says Allah made the sea bed dry. The thing blocking them became the road.
now: The illness that stops your career, the divorce that ends a whole life plan. It looks like the wall. {idea}Sometimes Allah opens a way straight through what is blocking you.{/idea} Do the small part in your hand, like Musa with his staff.
old: The obstacle in front of me is the end of the road.
new: Allah can turn the very obstacle into the path forward.
try: Do the one small action you can do about your problem today, and leave the rest to Allah.

title: The pursuers were drawn in after them.
subtitle: Following someone into a path not meant for you

row.title: the parted sea
sub: a path not meant for them

then: Ibn Abbas, Qatadah and others said this means {idea}We brought Fir'awn and his troops near to the sea.{/idea} He saw the open path and followed. {trap}He thought he was the hunter{/trap}, while Allah was bringing him exactly where his story would end.
now: You see someone succeed by a path that worked for them, and you rush after it without asking if it is yours. Or you chase someone to prove a point. {trap}Pride makes you walk into places you should never enter.{/trap}
old: If a path is open, I can follow it wherever it goes.
new: Not every open road is meant for me. Pride can lead me where I should not go.
try: Before your next big decision, ask: am I doing this for Allah or to prove something?

title: Every one of them crossed safely.
subtitle: Not one of the believers was lost
then: Allah says He saved Musa and those with him {reward}all together.{/reward} Ibn Kathir explains: We saved Musa and the Children of Israel and whoever followed their religion, {reward}and none of them were destroyed.{/reward} The same people who said we are caught all reached the other side.
now: The whole family got through the hard year. The team survived the layoffs. You were terrified, and then everyone made it. {reward}Remember that rescue.{/reward} Next time fear comes, bring that memory with you.
old: When things go well, it was probably luck.
new: The day everyone got through was Allah's rescue, and I should remember it.
try: Tell someone in your family about one time Allah got you all through something hard.

title: The same sea closed over the others.
subtitle: The end of Fir'awn and his army
then: Then Allah drowned the others. Ibn Kathir says {trap}Fir'awn and his troops were drowned and not one of them remained{/trap}. The whole government of Egypt that rode out that morning did not return. {idea}The same water that saved one group ended the other.{/idea}
now: The thing that rescues one person can ruin another: money, influence, a spotlight. It depends on what they do with it. {idea}Ask yourself which way your blessings are carrying you.{/idea}
old: Someone that powerful will always come out on top.
new: The same thing can save or ruin, depending on whose side I am on.
try: Pick one blessing you have, like money or influence, and use it today for something good.

title: A parted sea, and most still did not believe.
subtitle: The refrain after the story of Musa
then: The refrain returns after Musa's story. Ibn Kathir says this story, {idea}with its wonders and Allah's help to His believing servants{/idea}, is definitive proof of Allah's wisdom. A staff, a hand, a sea split in two. {trap}Yet most of them were not believers.{/trap}
now: You have seen your own parted seas: the recovery, the job that came at the last minute, the fight that ended in peace. {idea}How many more signs do you need?{/idea} The sign was never the problem.
old: If I had seen something like that, I would never doubt again.
new: Fir'awn saw the sea split. Signs do not make faith. The heart decides.
try: List three moments when Allah clearly helped you. Read the list when doubt comes.

title: Mighty with Fir'awn. Merciful with the magicians.
subtitle: Two names, two endings in one story
then: The second refrain closes Musa's story. Allah gave Fir'awn sign after sign and a long time in Egypt, and he refused. {idea}He is Mighty{/idea}: the army was ended in a moment. {reward}He is Merciful{/reward}: magicians who had served Fir'awn all their lives were welcomed in minutes.
now: You are somewhere between Fir'awn and the magicians right now. Maybe more stubborn than you want to admit. {reward}The magicians turned in a single afternoon.{/reward} The same Lord who is Mighty is waiting to be Merciful to you.
old: Either Allah is strict or He is forgiving. I am not sure which to expect.
new: He is both. His mercy is open to me today, before His might is needed.
try: Turn back to Allah today about one thing you have been stubborn about.

title: Now tell them the story of Ibrahim.
subtitle: The second story begins
then: Ibn Kathir says Allah {idea}commanded His Messenger Muhammad ﷺ to recite this story{/idea} to his Ummah so they could follow Ibrahim's example: {reward}sincerity towards Allah, putting trust in Him, and worshipping Him alone.{/reward} Ibrahim had been guided from a very early age.
now: You are looking for a role model. You follow people online who show you how to dress, eat, earn. {reward}Ibrahim is offered as the example for how to trust and how to stand alone.{/reward} His story is meant to be lived, not just admired.
old: Prophets' stories are inspiring history, not a guide for my life.
new: Ibrahim's story is given to me as an example to actually follow.
try: As you read the next verses, pick one thing Ibrahim does and copy it this week.

title: He starts at home: what do you worship?
subtitle: Ibrahim questions his father and his people
then: Ibrahim's first move is a question to {idea}his father and his people{/idea}: what do you worship? Ibn Kathir paraphrases it as: what are these statues to which you are so devoted? {idea}He begins by asking, not attacking.{/idea}
now: Your family spends hours on things you think are empty. You could lecture them. Ibrahim asked a question. {idea}What do you get out of this? What are we really living for?{/idea} A good question can open more than a speech.
old: To change my family, I need to tell them they are wrong.
new: A sincere question can reach further than a lecture.
try: Ask someone close to you one honest question about what matters most to them.

title: We worship idols, and we stay devoted to them.
subtitle: Proud devotion to something empty
then: They answered proudly: {trap}we worship idols, and to them we are ever devoted.{/trap} Ibn Kathir explains: we are devoted to worshipping them and praying to them. They were sincere, committed, faithful. {idea}Just to the wrong thing.{/idea}
now: You check the stock app forty times a day. You never miss the gym, the match, the series. You are deeply devoted. {idea}Devotion is not the question. What you are devoted to is.{/idea}
old: Being committed and consistent is what makes something good.
new: Devotion is only as good as what it is given to.
try: Check your screen time today. Ask honestly what you are most devoted to.

title: Do they even hear you when you call?
subtitle: Ibrahim's first test for any god
then: Ibrahim asks: {idea}do they hear you when you call?{/idea} The question is simple. Ibn Kathir notes that {trap}they knew their idols could not do anything.{/trap} A god who cannot hear you is not a god.
now: At 2 a.m. in the hospital waiting room, who do you call? Your bank balance does not hear you. Your follower count does not. {idea}Allah hears the call you whisper with no sound at all.{/idea}
old: The things I rely on will be there for me when I need them.
new: Only Allah truly hears me when I call in the dark.
try: Tonight, call on Allah in your own language about one need, even silently.

title: Can they help you? Can they even hurt you?
subtitle: Ibrahim's second test: real power
then: Ibrahim continues: {idea}do they benefit you, or do they cause harm?{/idea} Ibn Kathir says the people {trap}knew their idols could not do anything.{/trap} A thing that cannot help or harm cannot deserve worship.
now: You are afraid of what people will say, as if their opinion could ruin you. You chase approval as if it could save you. {idea}Ask Ibrahim's question: can it really help me? Can it really hurt me?{/idea}
old: What people think of me has the power to make or break me.
new: Only Allah can truly benefit or harm me. Everything else is borrowed.
try: Name one fear of people's opinion. Ask yourself: can they really harm me without Allah's will?

title: Our fathers did it. That is the whole argument.
subtitle: Tradition as a replacement for thinking
then: They could not say the idols hear or help. So they said {trap}we found our fathers doing so.{/trap} Ibn Kathir explains: they knew their idols could do nothing, but {trap}they had seen their fathers doing this, so they made haste to follow{/trap} in their footsteps.
now: At the wedding, the family insists on the expensive custom no one can afford. At work, it is just how it has always been done. {trap}That is how we have always done it is not a reason.{/trap} Keep the good of your elders, and check the rest.
old: If my family has always done it, it must be right.
new: Tradition is worth keeping when it is true, not just because it is old.
try: Pick one habit you do only because your family always did. Ask if it pleases Allah.

title: Have you really looked at what you worship?
subtitle: Ibrahim asks them to see clearly
then: After their answer about their fathers, Ibrahim says: {idea}then do you see what you have been worshipping?{/idea} He asks them to really look at the statues. Ibn Kathir says he was challenging them: if these idols {trap}have any influence, let them harm me.{/trap}
now: You have lived years on autopilot around something: a habit, a goal, a person you put above everything. {idea}Ibrahim's question is simple: have you actually looked at it?{/idea} Stop for a second and see it for what it is.
old: I know what I live for. I do not need to examine it.
new: Looking honestly at what I give my life to is the first step.
try: Take two minutes tonight and write what you spent most of your energy on this week.
